newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai traders sceptical about China rubber deal.
newsitem.headline: Thai traders sceptical about China rubber deal.

text.p: Thai traders and rubber authorities said on Wednesday they were puzzled by market talk that China may buy 80,000 tonnes of RSS3 rubber for delivery in the second half of this year.
A trader with a major local rubber firm, which has one of the largest market shares in China, said he had not heard of any such development from China so far.
"If China is interested to buy such an amount from Thailand, at least we should have heard about it since we have very good contacts and big market share there," he told Reuters.

"China is suffering from oversupply right now. Its import licence department is trying to control the amount of natural rubber imports. I would be very sceptical about the talk. Someone might be trying to push the market up," he added.
Others traders also expressed doubt but did not rule out the possibility that a deal could be in the works.

"Perhaps the deal is being negotiated on a government-to-government basis that we are not aware of. But I heard of no such development in the market. And if there is, it is a hush-hush deal. Actually, we heard this from Singapore, not here." said another Hat Yai-based trader.
Sanit Samosorn, deputy head of the Department of Agriculture, told Reuters that there had been no discussion between Thailand and China on a possible purchase of 80,000 tonnes of rubber.
"A few weeks ago, our minister went to China with some rubber exporters. If there is any deal done, it will be with the private sector," he said.

"The government did not discuss such a deal with China on a government-to-government basis," he added. Traders at the companies that went on the latest China trip said they had so far clinched no deal.
Talk that China may buy up to 80,000 tonnes of rubber from Thailand triggered speculative play for RSS3 rubber on Tuesday in the Singapore market.
In the market, only Japanese buyers featured while China kept a low profile.
Thai benchmark RSS3 was traded around 116.00 US cents a kg on an FOB basis this week for August delivery. September delivery was quoted around 117.50 US cents, traders said.
